purpose: Extend source-backed Module -> Practice -> Tool Task -> Evidence -> Review -> Rework -> Validation definitions from existing lesson activities.
rules: Definitions below translate existing Apply/Tool practice and Rework sections into gates.
No missing lesson content is invented.
Validation remains provisional until curriculum-level review.

modules.practice: Create/audit reusable patterns, tokens and components for one product flow; define purpose, anatomy and reusable decisions.
modules.toolTask: In Figma or Framer, build a mini system and/or audit five repeated patterns; extract tokens, define component states, document usage and refactor one flow.
review: System supports context rather than forcing identical screens
modules.validation: Learner can create and explain reusable design foundations and apply them consistently in context.

modules.practice: Define meaningful component states, responsive behaviour and documentation for one production component.
modules.toolTask: Create a state matrix, prototype transitions, test keyboard/touch/error paths, then document purpose, variants, states, constraints and accessibility.
modules.validation: Learner can specify a component's behaviour across states, contexts and responsive conditions and communicate it to another designer/builder.

modules.practice: Prepare a handoff package and perform design QA against intended design and implementation/prototype.
modules.toolTask: Create handoff for one flow in Figma/Framer; include context, states, responsive rules, assets, edge cases and open questions. Compare with implementation/prototype and maintain a QA log.
modules.validation: Learner can transfer design intent clearly and conduct actionable design QA beyond pixel comparison.

modules.practice: Turn a design question into a focused usability study and moderate a realistic task without leading participants.
modules.toolTask: Use a Figma/Framer prototype; create objective, participant/context, realistic task, neutral prompt, observation plan, debrief and moderator guide; pilot it.
review: Observed behaviour is separated from interpretation
modules.validation: Learner can plan and moderate a focused usability session while protecting the quality of evidence.

modules.practice: Turn observations into traceable findings, make an explicit prioritisation decision, and conduct evidence-based critique/rework.
modules.toolTask: Synthesize a Figma/Framer test into 3–5 findings; define prioritisation criteria and trade-offs; critique a screen/flow and create V2.
modules.validation: Learner can transform research evidence into defensible findings, transparent decisions and actionable design rework.

modules.practice: Define task success, time, meaningful errors, assistance and confidence measures before testing a prototype.
modules.toolTask: Run a usability measurement exercise in Figma/Framer and create an observation sheet; separate evidence from interpretation and proposed changes.
modules.validation: Learner can use task-based usability measures alongside observation and participant feedback to identify patterns and questions.

modules.practice: Map content to user tasks, audit hierarchy and identify missing/error/empty states before polishing copy.
modules.toolTask: Create a content map for one flow, prototype improved hierarchy and compare V1/V2 with a short usability check.
modules.validation: Learner can treat content as part of the interface and structure information around user needs.

modules.practice: Audit and rewrite interface labels/messages for action, context, consequence, tone, accessibility and task clarity.
modules.toolTask: In Figma/Framer, identify five microcopy items (CTA, hint, error, confirmation, empty state), rewrite them and test realistic lengths.
review: Copy remains usable at realistic lengths
modules.validation: Learner can produce task-focused interface language that reduces uncertainty and remains usable in context.

modules.practice: Choose a product task, define the UX question and outcome, then select quantitative and qualitative evidence with baseline/context and guardrails.
modules.toolTask: Create an annotated Figma/Framer flow showing where evidence could be collected and what result would trigger investigation.
review: Qualitative and quantitative evidence complement each other
Correlation is not treated as causation
modules.validation: Learner can connect UX questions to appropriate evidence and avoid treating a single metric as proof of design success.

modules.practice: Audit a previously designed flow for broad accessibility and inclusive-design considerations, then rework identified barriers.
modules.toolTask: Use Figma/Framer to annotate perceivable/operable/understandable/robust considerations, contrast, cognitive load and inclusive needs.
review: Inclusive considerations are tied to user/context needs
Assumptions are distinguished from validated findings
modules.validation: Learner demonstrates accessibility/inclusive design reasoning in an actual interface rather than only recalling principles.

modules.practice: Create and execute a multi-method accessibility validation plan for a key product flow.
modules.toolTask: Map focus order and semantic/content structure in Figma/Framer; define automated, keyboard, zoom/text, assistive-technology and user-evidence checks where applicable.
modules.validation: Learner can plan and interpret multi-method accessibility validation without overclaiming from a single test.
